packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-06 - unverified blind image reading (reader D)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification or earlier reading of this fragment was in my
  context.
- The host printed book is partly visible beside the fragment (an alphabet /
  signature register page with "...ARTARVM." in capitals); I did not use it.
- Beyond the brief: I cut each tile into left/right halves in my scratchpad
  folder (readerD/) to view them closer to native size. No other files.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 (overview, upright) and image-005 (same object, rotated 90 deg):
  parchment spine-lining strips glued across the spine of a sewn text block,
  three panels separated by two raised sewing supports (bands with
  thread wrapping). Sewing threads pierce the strips top and bottom.
- Upper and middle panels (image-002, image-003, image-004): text reads
  horizontally in image-001. Main text block of c. 18-20 letters per visible
  line, written in a small gothic book hand, brown ink, heavy abbreviation.
  To its left, separated by a blank intercolumn with a ruled line, a narrow
  strip of a SECOND column (line ends only, c. 8-10 letters). So the leaf was
  at least two columns; the visible main block is the right-hand column, its
  right edge partly lost to the strip edge.
- Lower panel (image-006, image-007): text runs vertically in image-001,
  horizontally in image-005 and the tiles; another part of the same or a
  sister leaf, same hand. A second, overlapping piece of parchment lies over
  the lower part (visible step in image-007 around line 10).
- Marginal note at right of the middle panel (image-004): a capital A with
  "dexi?" / "trans?" written beneath in a cursive hand (could be a later
  annotation or a quire/section mark; uncertain).
- Paraphs/line marks: none certain. No rubrics in colour visible; no
  enlarged initials. Text appears to be continuous prose with question-
  and-answer markers ("R(espo)n(sio)", "2(°)", "Item") - tentative.
- Overlap: image-003 bottom lines repeat at the top of image-004 (lines
  "[..]erpo p(ro)p(ter) mala..." to "[..] q(uod) qui regit..."). Treated as
  overlap, not new text. image-006 last lines repeat at the top of image-007.

TRANSCRIPTION
Conventions: (x) expansion; x? uncertain reading; [illegible]; line numbers
count text lines from the top of the named image.

AREAS READ / UNREAD
- Read: all visible lines of the three panels, but many words are only
  partly secure. Most secure lines: image-003 l.6 ("q(ui) (con)fitet(ur)
  debeat de o(mn)ib(us) peccatis suis (con)fiteri."), l.7 ("R(espo)n(sio)
  q(uod) sic."), image-004 l.9 ("ne sacerdos reuelet (con)fessione(m)
  mea(m)"), image-004 l.11 ("peccatu(m) alicui reuel..."), image-006 l.2
  ("...st p(ro)fessionis . et i(n) hac l..."), image-003 l.2 ("lazar(us)
  suscitat(us)").
- Unread: text under the sewing bands and threads; the right ends of main-
  column lines lost at the strip edge; the hidden other side of the strips
  (pasted down); text under the overlapping second piece in image-007.

LIMITATIONS
- Heavy abbreviation; several expansions (e.g. "catet", "absoluete",
  "Ter") are only letter-shape guesses. Column relation of the lower panel to
  the upper panels is unknown (may be a different leaf or a different face).
- Suggest: tiles of the lower panel at higher magnification, raking light
  for the abraded middle portions, and imaging under the sewing bands if
  conservation ever lifts the linings.
